trials.notes: Used the correct HTML Processor fragment parser and the documented token-rewrite pattern: next_token(), #text guard, get_modifiable_text() for decoded comparison, and serialize_token() inside trusted wrapper markup. All HTML API calls are present in the rendered docs and execution recorded no _doing_it_wrong notices. Minor deduction only for broad fallback branches that may return normalized/raw original input on processor creation failure rather than a task-specific normalized rewrite policy.

Used the intended WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() flow and documented token serialization APIs. All HTML API methods used are documented, with no _doing_it_wrong notices. The main adherence weakness is the get_last_error() fallback: after emitting a rewrite, it returns WP_HTML_Processor::normalize( $html ) ?? $html, which the serialize_token docs explicitly warn discards accumulated token-loop changes and may return unnormalized original input.

Correct processor choice and mostly idiomatic token walking: #text tokens are compared through decoded get_modifiable_text() and emitted through serialize_token(). All API methods used, including get_token_name() and is_tag_closer(), are documented and no _doing_it_wrong notices appeared. Deductions are for an unnecessary special-element branch that calls get_modifiable_text() even though the task excludes that opener-carried text, plus the same normalize-original fallback risk after a token rewrite.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all 8 hidden cases, so there were no failed hidden cases to attribute to documentation gaps. The rendered docs did especially well on the critical distinctions for this task: the processor-selection guidance says to use WP_HTML_Processor for structure, missing/implied closing tags, and normalized output; the rewrite-while-serializing recipe and serialize_token() docs describe accumulating token output and wrapping serialize_token(); get_modifiable_text() documents decoded text for #text nodes; and the ordinary-text guidance warns that comments, attributes, and special-element opener text are not ordinary #text descendants. Those passages map directly to the entity, comment, attribute, split-node, and normalization cases. The near misses were around fallback policy and special elements: trial-2 and trial-3 still used normalize( $html ) ?? $html in an error branch after building rewrite output, and trial-3 defensively read special-element opener text even though it did not need it. These did not affect the hidden cases, but they show where the docs could make the successful pattern more obviously complete.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn that normalize( $html ) after a token loop discards emitted changes, but candidates still used it in error branches as a generic fallback.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short contract-oriented fallback note: once a token rewrite has emitted output, fallback to normalize() or raw input is an explicit decision to discard the rewrite; string-returning filters should document whether they return best-effort accumulated output, an empty string, null, or the original input on unsupported markup.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain that SCRIPT/STYLE/TITLE/TEXTAREA text is carried on the opener token, but may leave readers thinking they must call get_modifiable_text() on those openers to preserve or skip the content.
doc_gaps.suggestion: State explicitly that no read call is needed to advance past or serialize special-element contents: serialize_token() on the opener preserves the token, and a #text-only filter naturally excludes opener-carried special text.

doc_gaps.problem: Processor creation failure and later parser aborts are documented separately, but examples leave fallback policy to the caller, which can produce inconsistent normalized-vs-raw behavior in string APIs.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Include a compact example of a string-returning API choosing one fallback policy consistently for both create_fragment() returning null and get_last_error() becoming non-null, without implying that raw input is normalized output.
